title: The k-th Smallest Key

concept.title: The in-order walk of a search tree is sorted
body: Because the left subtree holds the smaller values and the right subtree the larger ones, the **in-order** walk (left, node, right) of a BST visits the values in **increasing order**. So the `k`-th smallest value is the `k`-th node visited by the in-order walk, and the walk can stop as soon as that node is reached.

body.code:
def kth_smallest(root, k):
    stack = []
    cur = root
    while stack or cur is not None:
        while cur is not None:           # go as far left as possible
            stack.append(cur)
            cur = cur.left
        cur = stack.pop()                # the next smallest value
        k -= 1
        if k == 0:
            return cur.val
        cur = cur.right

body: This version uses an explicit **stack** instead of recursion: the stack holds the nodes whose left subtree is being visited. It also works for very deep trees where the recursion would be too deep, and it stops early, visiting only `k` nodes plus the nodes on the way down.

statement: Given a binary search tree and a number `k`, print the `k`-th smallest value in the tree (the smallest value is the 1st).
inputFormat: The first line has `t`, the number of words in the description of the tree.
The second line has the tree in level order: the root first, then the children of the nodes row by row from left to right. `N` stands for a missing child. There is no `N` at the end.
constraints: The height of the tree is at most 800.
The tree is a binary search tree (all values are different).

examples.note: The values in increasing order are 1 2 3 4 6 7 9; the 3rd is 3.

hints: The in-order walk of a search tree gives the values in increasing order.
Count the visited nodes and stop at the k-th one.
An explicit stack (or recursion with a counter) does the walk.
